paper_title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World Software Engineering Problems?
core_problem: Evaluating language models on complex, real-world software engineering tasks that require editing entire codebases and resolving issue descriptions.
methodology_summary: Introduces SWE-bench, an evaluation framework consisting of 2,294 software engineering problems from 12 Python repositories. The methodology constructs prompts via sparse or dense retrieval over codebases and evaluates model-generated code patches using repository unit testing frameworks.
empirical_results: Evaluated state-of-the-art language models fail to solve all except a small fraction of instances, demonstrating that real-world software engineering tasks remain extremely challenging for existing models.
explicit_limitations: Task instances are strictly in Python; evaluations only establish simple baseline retrieval methods without agent-based or tool-augmented setups; relying solely on execution-based testing does not guarantee code readability, efficiency, or comprehensiveness.
